newsitem.title: USA: 3M sees $500 mln in drug system sales by 2000.
newsitem.headline: 3M sees $500 mln in drug system sales by 2000.

text.p: Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing said Wednesday it expects $500 million in sales by the year 2000 from three new drug deliver systems.

Pharmaceuticals division vice president Tom Harrison said the company could expect $350 million in sales by the year 2000 from CFC-free inhalers, $50 million from the Estrogen patch and $100 million from the Imiquimod topical treatment for genital warts.
"We expect $500 million in sales by 2000 from these products, with returns well above the 3M average," Harrison told analysts Wednesday. He did not say what that average was.
The company had $600 million in pharmaceutical sales in 1995.
The company's CFC-free inhaler was introduced overseas in 1995 and received FDA approval on August 16.
The seven-day Estrogen patch was launched in 1995 and has a 20 percent sahre of the transdermal Estrogen repalcement therapy market in the United States.
U.S. introduction of the Imiquimod treatment is planned for 1997, pending approval, Harrison said.
